messages.subject: Initial values issue
parts:
Hello,

I am using the V-dem measurement model (recently posted different questions for the same model):

data {
  int<lower=2> K; // categories
  int<lower=0> J; // raters
  int<lower=0> N; // N country-years
  int<lower=0> C; // countries
  int<lower=-2,upper=10> wdata[N,J]; // data
  int<lower=1,upper=C> cdata[J]; // j country indices
  real gsigmasq; // rater-level gamma variance around country-level gammas
  real gsigmasqc; // country-level gamma variance around world gammas
  // vector [N] mc;
}
parameters {
  real Z;
  // instead of vector[N] Z;
  ordered[K-1] gamma[J];
  vector[K-1] gamma_mu; // world-level cutpoints
  matrix[C,(K-1)] gamma_c; // country-level cuts, rows are countries
  real<lower=0> beta[J]; // reliability score
}
model{
  vector[K] p;
  real left;
  real right;
  Z ~ normal(0,1); // vague prior
  // Z[i] ~ normal(mc[i],1);
  gamma_mu ~ uniform(-2,2);
  for (c in 1:C) {
    gamma_c[c] ~ normal(gamma_mu,gsigmasqc); // row-access of gamma_c
  }
  for (j in 1:J) {
    gamma[j] ~ normal(gamma_c[cdata[j]],gsigmasq); // note row-access
    beta[j] ~ normal(1,1)T[0,]; // truncated so that > 0
    for (i in 1:N) if (wdata[i,j] != -1) {
        left <- 0;
        for (k in 1:(K-1)) {
          right <- left;
          left <- Phi_approx(gamma[j,k]-Z*beta[j]); // fast approximation to Phi
          p[k] <- left - right;
        }
        p[K] <- 1.0 - left;
        wdata[i,j] ~ categorical(p);
      }
    }
  }

The problem is that occasionally some chains fail to initialise and start sampling, generating the following message: "Rejecting initial value: Log probability evaluates to log(0), i.e. negative infinity."

I have two questions: (a) Any idea which of the model's variables might create the problem here? (b) How do I set initial values for my variables?

I am using RStan:

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: Initial values issue
parts:
Hi Panos, you can specify initial values with RStan using the init argument. I think the doc is a little clearer in version 2.10 (I see you're using version 2.9), but you can specify a list or a function. From the stan function help page (see the Examples section on that page too): 

List:
 
A list equal in length to the number of chains. The elements of this list should themselves be named lists, where each of these named lists has the name of a parameter and is used to specify the initial values for that parameter for the corresponding chain.
 
Function: 

A function that returns a list for specifying the initial values of parameters for a chain. The function can take an optional parameter chain_id through which the chain_id (if specified) or the integers from 1 to chains will be supplied to the function for generating initial values.


Also, it's ok to specify initial values for only some parameters, leaving the rest to be generated by Stan.


Jonah
